headline: Claude joins your meetings, Gemini's free tier levels up
summary: Two things you can actually use today: Claude takes meeting notes for you, and Gemini's free model jumps a tier.

items.title: Claude joins the meeting room: automatic notes
items.pitch: Claude can join a Google Meet as a participant, listen and take notes as it goes, and when the call ends the notes and action items stay in Claude.
why: No more scribbling in meetings — notes and to-dos are ready when the call ends
Notes land right in Claude, so you can pick up and edit a doc
The team can watch what it writes in real time and correct it on the spot
actions: Connect Google Meet in Claude and try it on your next call
Have it open a doc during a meeting and watch it listen and write
deep_dive: Different from the meeting tools you use now: Claude actually joins the call as a participant, not just records and transcribes.
Right now it only supports Google Meet; other platforms are said to be coming; the team plan gives the fuller experience.
Honest take: it can get things wrong and needs a human to correct it, so skip it for sensitive meetings for now.
items.signals: Official @claudeai posted 3 times · top post hit 1,678 likes · Dan Shipper tried it live

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: a big free-tier upgrade
items.pitch: Google's new cheap, fast model is already in the Gemini app and is now the default engine for AI in Google Search.
why: 5 percentage points more accurate than the last Flash (measured by Box)
Same task takes less than half the time, with 12% fewer tokens
Free users and Search users get this upgrade automatically
actions: Open the Gemini app, pick Hydrogen and throw a few questions at it
Check whether the AI answers in Google Search got more accurate
deep_dive: Cheaper and faster than Carbon/Argon — it's the workhorse for everyday chores, not the one you throw hard problems at.
Carbon/Argon prices double after December 1, which is when Hydrogen's cheapness really shows; right now the price gap is small.
Honest take: the free tier still isn't the paid flagship, so don't expect complex analysis from it.
items.signals: Two HN posts at 536 and 428 points · Simon Willison tested it · Box CEO measured +5 points accuracy

items.title: Edge0-145B: frontier models on your own machine
items.pitch: A new model claims it can deliver "frontier" capability locally on a personal computer, keeping your data and privacy on your own machine.
why: Runs locally, so your data never goes to the cloud
But 145B is a memory hog — a normal computer can't handle it
